November 2025 Report
                            Girdwood Trails Committee

Updates and other business:
Girdwood Parks Master Plan is now underway. Public workshop Sept 16 received input. Upcoming is an Advisory
Committee meeting to review recommendations compiled after the workshop, stakeholders, survey and staff. Next
public meeting is tentatively scheduled for Dec 16  www.girdwoodparksplan.com.
Girdwood Valley Trails Management Plan. Current version is posted on the GTC page. Barb Crews has initiated review
of this document with the goal of updating it to match the Girdwood Trails Master Plan. Review the amendments:
https://www.muni.org/Departments/operations/streets/Service/Trails/Girdwood%20Trails%20Management%20Plan%
20REV%20DRAFT%20Intro%20thru%20Chapter%204.pdf
Girdwood Trails Master Plan. Adopted version is posted on the GTC page. GirdwoodTrailsPlan_February2024.pdf
Girdwood Comprehensive Plan. Final version was formally adopted in early April 2025.

Financial report: $26,507.81. RTP reimbursement #1 of $42,935 received Oct 31.

Trail Projects: Status of GVSA Trails projects slated for 2025:
    •   Bridge replacement over California Creek adjacent to Town Square Park/Crow Creek Road funded by private
        donation.      IN PROGRESS. Delay with permitting, project construction 2026
    •   Tread work on Virgin Creek Falls Trail funded by private donation assisting with YEP crew. COMPLETE!
    •    Trail work and trailhead signage on the Lower Virgin Creek Trail (a social trail that connects Virgin Creek Road
        to Danich Trail). PENDING
    •   Bidding for Suspension bridge to replace the Hand Tram funded by a variety of sources. Build expected in
      2026 to provide time for material acquisition.  PENDING
    •   Tread and drainage work on the Middle Iditarod National Historic Trail between the school and USFS Boundary
       co-funded by GVSA and RTP Grant COMPLETE; next steps are platting and reroute/construction of trail
       segment.
    •   Construction of a pavilion in Lions Club Park, co-funded by GVSA, Lions Club, private donations and LWCF
        grant. PENDING
    •   Study storm damage to the Beaver Pond Trail/make repairs. COMPLETE

Grants Status report:
Alaska Community Foundation: Girdwood Parks and Rec applied for Trail Care grant and was awarded $1000 for trail
backpack and chainsaw for trail work. Funds received and given to Girdwood Inc for GTC Account.
State of Alaska, Capital Budget: Thank you to Alaska Trails for including the suspension bridge to replace the Hand
Tram in their requests for funding of the State of Alaska. State has awarded $1.2M for this project as part of Alaska
Long Trail Funding.
Rasmuson Tier II Grant: GVSA has been awarded funding for this project.
Recreational Trails Program Grant (RTP): RTP grant for 2026 has been announced. GTC did not apply. 2024 grant
was awarded for the Middle INHT. Delays pushed it to 2025, wrapping up reimbursement.
Dugan Family donation for trails signs on Middle Iditarod Trail and bench at the 5K parking are nearing completion.
Remaining is the trail sign that will be produced and placed.
Dugan Family donation for reconstruction of 2 bridges on the Middle Iditarod Trail; PROJECT COMPLETE These bridges
are complete!
Private funder has donated funds for new bridge to connect Crow Creek Road to town center behind ACS building.
Trail Map Project: Summer map project complete and printed. Winter map project is under way.
Trails Commercial Use Permits: 2025 permits are being issued by Girdwood Parks and Recreation. Any business
operating commercially on Girdwood public land and trails should have a permit issued locally. Contact for requesting
permits is girdwoodpermits@anchorageak.gov 907-343-8373. Report operators without permits to Kyle Kelley:
kyle.kelley@anchorageak.gov 907-343-8374.

Summer Trails Projects
         •   Glacier Creek Bridge on Winner Creek Trail

         •   Middle Iditarod NHT                                Upgrades complete to USFS Boundary
              Platting of Trail easement
            Reroute of trail at HH

         •   Pedestrian Bridge on California Creek connecting town center to Crow Creek Road
              Privately funded re-build at 50% design currently.        Securing permitting
                                                                    Construction 2026

         •    Virgin Creek Falls Trail tread work                    2025 successful work with YEP
                                                         2026 Continue with adding gravel

         •   Beaver Pond Trail                                2025 successful tree clearing/drainage
                                                         2026 more drainage and tread work

         •   Storm repair/Winter clean-up/Maintenance
         TBD

         •   Lower Virgin Creek Trail (from Virgin Creek Road)       2026 initiate projects
                Install Trailhead post
             Clear blowdowns
             Establish route to the bench to deter meandering trail on the sidehill
          Work on getting an easement for the trail

         •    Installation of trail map sign at 5K parking

  From: Dipaola-Allen, Justin A (DNR) <justin.dipaola-allen@alaska.gov>
  Sent: Thursday, September 4, 2025 2:57 PM
  To: Tyler, Margaret S. <margaret.tyler@anchorageak.gov>
  Cc: Wedeking, Matthew D (DNR) <matthew.wedeking@alaska.gov>
  Subject: Re: Request for Chugach State Park RTP grant project



 [EXTERNAL EMAIL]

  Hi Margaret,

  Please share the note below with the GTC board.

  Girdwood Trails Committee Board,

  Thank you for the thoughtful letter and for the Girdwood Trails Committee’s steady advocacy for
  the Bird-to-Gird. I share your concerns about safety, drainage, and sightlines.

  Good news: Alaska DOT&PF has an active Seward Highway project, MP 90–99 (CFHWY00850),
  that includes repairs and upgrades to trail facilities in this corridor. The scope targets avalanche
  and water damage and is intended to extend the life of both the highway and the path. Because this
  work is already programmed with DOT&PF, Chugach State Park is not planning to pursue a 2026
 RTP application for this need.

  In the near term, Parks will continue routine brushing and drainage maintenance to support safety
  until DOT&PF completes its project. We’re also acquiring additional mechanized vegetation-
  clearing capacity and have identified the Bird-to-Gird as a Summer 2026 top priority.

  Thank you again for the offer of a GBOS resolution; I’ll be sure to pass your perspective along to
 DOT&PF.

  Best,

Justin

___________________

Justin DiPaola-Allen

Superintendent

Chugach State Park

Alaska State Parks

907-444-3980
